The {{n_reports}} reports

genomic-benchmarks-qc renders a self-contained report for every unit it measures: one per split per sequence column for the {{n_split_checks_word}} class-distribution checks, and one per split pair for the leakage scan. There are {{n_reports}} of them across {{n_datasets}} datasets.

{{report_state}} {{route_note}}

They are downloaded, not committed, and there is one copy of them. The archives are 90 MB and unpack to far more, so a clone does not carry them; gb-audit fetch brings them from Zenodo straight into the built site, at the address this page links to. Nothing stages or copies them anywhere else, so the record is the only place they come from.

data/reports.csv records each archive's size, digest and every path inside it. That is how this page can list what exists whether or not it was downloaded, and how each archive is checked before it is unpacked: an archive whose bytes are not the bytes the manifest describes is refused rather than published.

What each report holds

Class distributions
What the nine class-distribution checks found on one split, for one sequence column: the distribution of each feature by class, the probe fits, and the per-position profiles. A dataset with two sequence columns gets one report per column.
Leakage scan
The comparison of one pair of splits: the sequence matches found, and the individual sequences of one split that were also present in the other. This is the report that makes an overlapping held-out sequence identifiable rather than only countable.
